A.justification: A builds a complete, working feature the way webERP does it. The upgrade script uses the CreateTable and NewScript helpers, there is a matching install-schema table and scripts.sql rows, and the maintenance page closely follows AddCustomerNotes.php: FormID, __() strings, delete confirm, and session.php's input escaping used as intended. Its dates work with the HTML date input, because FormatDateForSQL passes Y-m-d through unchanged. It also handles side effects the reference misses: Stocks.php now deletes an item's notes before deleting the item, and Z_ChangeStockCode.php moves notes to the new code, so the new foreign key does not break either flow. The import is a separate Z_ImportStockNotes.php linked from Z_ImportStocks.php. It escapes values the same way session.php does and supports many notes per item. Its only gap against the checklist is that Z_ImportStocks.php itself does not take a notes column.

Z_ChangeStockCode.php leaves notes under the old stock code (FK checks are disabled there), orphaning them
B.justification: B has the right overall shape: an upgrade script using the helpers, an install table, scripts.sql registration, a menu link, a CRUD page and a separate notes importer. The page has a real runtime bug, though. It escapes $_POST['Note'] again even though session.php has already applied DB_escape_string and htmlspecialchars. As a result, multi-line notes are stored with literal backslash-n text, and apostrophes and other special characters are shown double-encoded. Editing a note re-encodes it every time, and notes entered through the form end up stored differently from imported ones. It also does not update Stocks.php or Z_ChangeStockCode.php for the new foreign-key table, so deleting an item that has notes fails and changing its stock code orphans its notes. On conventions, it registers a page that writes data at the inquiry token 2, puts concatenated text inside __() in the importer, and builds a simpler form that does not use the field/label structure of the existing notes scripts. Like A, it handles import in a separate script instead of extending Z_ImportStocks.php.
